tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to check...'), focuses on user intent (security assessment, specific questions users might ask like 'are my notebooks exposed to the internet?'), explicitly lists trigger contexts (notebooks, Studio domains, models, endpoints, training/processing jobs, Feature Store, Model Monitor, Model Registry), and includes a clear disambiguation from a related skill. It is concise given the scope it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to check whether their Amazon SageMaker AI setup is secure: a security assessment, audit, posture review or hardening check of notebooks, Studio domains, models, endpoints, training/processing jobs, Feature Store, Model Monitor or Model Registry, or asks about one SageMaker security setting, such as "are my notebooks exposed to the internet?"

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays domain-specific throughout — it explains SageMaker-specific conventions (verifiability classification, multi-region/account handling, read-only guardrails) rather than general concepts the agent already knows. No filler explaining what security assessments or AWS APIs are in general terms.
tests.evidence: **Verifiable** — a read-only `Describe`/`List` returns the exact configuration... **Heuristic** — readable, but the verdict is an inference...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, API docs, or error code lists are embedded in the body; the 25 checks and their logic are explicitly deferred to references/sagemaker-checks.md. Conditional branches (e.g., SM-02 mixed check) are short, high-level rules rather than detailed data dumps.
tests.evidence: Open [references/sagemaker-checks.md](references/sagemaker-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the read-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, verifiability, resolution text...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/safety-critical sections (read-only guardrail, verifiability contract) are highly prescriptive with exact rules and exceptions, while less fragile areas (e.g., scope determination, account confirmation) allow flexibility. This matches the fragility of each operation well.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... Treat every account as production unless told otherwise.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple interchangeable tools/approaches for the same task; it specifies one consistent read-only API approach throughout.
tests.evidence: ONLY call `Describe*`, `List*`, `Get*`, `BatchGet*`, and equivalent read operations.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (confirm scope, resolve regions, run checks per region/account, assemble report, self-check) applicable to any SageMaker security assessment request, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence: Work through these steps in order. Treat each box as a gate — do not move on until it is satisfied: ... Step 1 — Confirm intent and scope.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes substantial gotcha-like guidance throughout (e.g., verify vs prescribe contract, SM-02 mixed check nuance, multi-account assume-role caveat) covering non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: **`SM-02` is a mixed check.** Its AmazonSageMakerFullAccess detection is **Heuristic**... Do not call `Generate*`, report those aspects as prescribe guidance in the resolution.
